title: What If All the Bats Vanished? Farmers Would Notice First

scenes.text: What if every bat vanished tonight? Your dinner would be the first thing to change.
Bats eat enormous numbers of insects. One colony of 150 big brown bats eats about 1.3 million a year.
Many of those insects destroy crops. A 2011 study in Science valued bats at billions of dollars a year to farmers.
The estimate runs from 3.7 billion up to 53 billion dollars a year, and that counts the pesticide farmers would no longer need.
Without bats, pesticide use goes up. Farmers would have to spray more to protect the same crops.
And it's not hypothetical. White-nose syndrome has already killed more than a million bats in the Northeast.

description:
What if all the bats vanished?
Insect-eating bats save farmers billions of dollars a year, and in the Northeast a fungus has already killed over a million.
